apiEntry.intro: Cashier devices (WPF / handheld / iPad) reach the POS API through three routes: EdgeOne, AWS Sydney and Direct to Singapore. All three lead to the same backend. Pick the preferred route for each store here; the other two act as fallbacks automatically: if the preferred route is unreachable the device switches to the next one at once, and switches back after recovery. Changes take effect within about 1 minute (slower at night), with no restart and no impact on payments in progress.

modeDescriptions.edge: Tencent multi-node acceleration; billed per request.
modeDescriptions.aws: Self-hosted Sydney edge with warm connections and fast first requests; network independent of Tencent; single server.
modeDescriptions.direct: Straight to the Singapore origin with no middle layer; unstable on a few ISPs.

apiUsage.intro: Counts requests from POS devices to the POS API, split by route (EdgeOne / AWS Sydney / Direct). The server identifies the route from where each request arrived; devices report nothing. Dates use Sydney time and weeks start on Monday. Data refreshes about once a minute and starts accumulating after release; history cannot be backfilled.

apiUsage.mainIntro: Counts requests to the main API (the /api endpoints used by the web back office and the staff app), split by route (EdgeOne / AWS Sydney / Direct) and by client type (Web back office / Staff app / Other). The origin server identifies the route; the client type is a rough split from the request's browser identifier, and only counts are stored - never the identifier text, IP or user. Dates use Sydney time and weeks start on Monday. Data refreshes about once a minute and starts accumulating after release; history cannot be backfilled. Until the origin server is configured to mark the route, all requests show as Unidentified.
